subtitle: Monthly horror picks for the mortally curious.
vote_instructions: Vote for as many novels as you're interested in.

novels.title: Red Dragon
novels.author: Thomas Harris (1981)
novels.vibe: The procedural that invented the modern serial-killer thriller, cold and clinical right up until it isn't.
novels.summary: Retired FBI profiler Will Graham is pulled back into the field to catch the “Tooth Fairy,” a killer who murders entire families under the light of the full moon. To understand the killer's mind, Graham has to consult the one man who understands it best: Hannibal Lecter, the imprisoned psychiatrist whose capture nearly destroyed him. The book that introduced Lecter to readers, it's less about gore than the slow, disquieting intimacy of hunting a mind like your own.
novels.warnings: Graphic violence, murder of children and families, child abuse (backstory), sexual violence, animal death, mental illness portrayed as monstrous.

novels.title: Clown in a Cornfield
novels.author: Adam Cesare (2020)
novels.vibe: Small-town generational rage with a killer clown mascot and a body count that escalates fast.
novels.summary: Quinn Maybrook moves with her father to a dying Missouri town just in time for its Founder's Day festival, and for the local mascot, Frendo the clown, to start murdering teenagers with farm equipment. What starts as slasher-movie fun curdles into something angrier, as the killings turn out to be an organized reckoning between the town's adults and its kids. Fast, mean, and very aware of the slasher rules it's both following and breaking.
novels.warnings: Graphic violence and gore, gun violence, bullying, drug references, suicidal ideation, child endangerment.

novels.title: I Was a Teenage Slasher
novels.author: Stephen Graham Jones (2024)
novels.vibe: A slasher told from inside the killer's own head, equal parts elegy and body count.
novels.summary: Tolly Driver is a quiet, overlooked seventeen-year-old in 1989 Lamesa, Texas, until one violent night rewires him into something else entirely, and he starts a summer-long killing spree he can't fully control. Narrated decades later by Tolly himself, looking back with real grief and real menace, it's a slasher novel that loves and dissects the genre from the inside — sympathetic to its “final girl” structure even as it centers the monster.
novels.warnings: Graphic violence and gore, teen death, homophobia, racism, animal death, self-loathing/dissociation.

novels.title: The Butterfly Garden
novels.author: Dot Hutchison (2016)
novels.vibe: A serial predator's private garden of captive girls, told in an interrogation room after the fire.
novels.summary: FBI agents interview a survivor known only as Maya after a raid on a hidden compound called the Garden, where a man known as the Gardener has spent years collecting young women, tattooing their backs with butterfly wings, and killing them the moment they show signs of aging. Maya's account, told in fragments across the interrogation, reconstructs the Garden's twisted rules and the girls who tried to survive them. Less slasher chase than slow-burn captivity horror, built around a collector's calm, controlling brand of serial violence.
novels.warnings: Child sexual abuse, rape, kidnapping and captivity, murder, forced tattooing, grooming, suicidal ideation.
